name: Invenergy LLC (Invenergy Renewables Holdings LLC · Invenergy Renewables LLC · Invenergy Clean Power LLC · Invenergy Transmission LLC · Invenergy Power)
headquarters: Chicago, Illinois (street address not published on the pages read); development offices in the US, Canada, Mexico, Spain, Japan, Poland and Scotland per the June 2023 Blackstone release
employees: '2,800+ people' per invenergy.com (September 2026); workforce-data aggregators show lower estimates (about 2,460–2,575) that no primary source confirms
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Invenergy is the second-largest US developer by development pipeline on Cleanview's live rankings (41,328 MW across 212 projects, behind NextEra Energy's 68,229 MW and ahead of Engie and Intersect), which makes it the largest non-utility developer on that measure — the 'largest privately held' phrase is Invenergy's and Blackstone's own language, not an independent ranking, and the ranking measure is pipeline megawatts, not operating capacity. The company is owned by CDPQ (52.4% economic ownership of Invenergy Renewables LLC after May 2018, invested since 2013), Blackstone Infrastructure Partners (about USD 3 billion in January 2022 plus about USD 1 billion in June 2023 into Invenergy Renewables Holdings LLC, 'approximately $4 billion' combined) and management, with 'CDPQ and Invenergy management' stated as majority owners and Invenergy as managing member; no 2024–2026 stake sale, recapitalisation or valuation appears in any release, filing or reputable report read. Its storage business is real but small relative to the whole and is disclosed only in fragments: '27 projects developed', '5,000 megawatt-hours of storage developed' and '150 utility-scale projects in the storage development pipeline' per the company, 736 MW of Arizona storage operating or under construction per Salt River Project (March 2026), and about 2.4 GW of named development-stage microsites in Arizona, Iowa, Tennessee, Ohio, New Mexico and Maryland. The strategic centre of gravity in 2025–2026 is elsewhere: a new Invenergy Power unit (April 2026) for 'natural gas and data center development', 1,800 MW of Meta contracts, a 918 MW gas plant sold to AEP's Indiana Michigan Power, about 3.3 GW of Wisconsin gas plants proposed for We Energies' data-centre load, a USD 765 million federal buyout of four offshore-wind leases (June 2026) redirected to gas and geothermal, and the privately financed USD 11 billion Grain Belt Express HVDC line after the Department of Energy terminated its USD 4.9 billion conditional loan guarantee in July 2025.

BACKGROUND. Founded in Chicago in 2001 by Michael Polsky (who sold SkyGen Energy to Calpine that year) with Jim Murphy, Invenergy describes itself as 'North America's largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of innovative, reliable power infrastructure', with 'over 220 projects totaling more than 38 gigawatts' developed and 'over 25 gigawatts' operated across four continents per its May 2026 boilerplate; earlier boilerplate (April 2026) said 36 GW developed and 20 GW operated, and the figures move release to release. The business spans onshore wind, solar, standalone and hybrid storage, natural gas, transmission (Grain Belt Express, Cimarron Link, New Mexico North Path, the completed Cardal line in Uruguay), clean hydrogen (Sauk Valley, Illinois, operating since March 2025) and affiliates — Invenergy Services (operations), Illuminate USA (a 1.1 million-square-foot solar-module plant in Pataskala, Ohio, 'over 1,600 associates'), Reactivate and Energize Capital. Structure per the company's own releases: Invenergy Renewables Holdings LLC is the vehicle Blackstone invested in; Invenergy Renewables LLC carries CDPQ's stake; Invenergy Clean Power LLC holds the gas portfolio in a 2018 50/50 partnership with AMP Capital (now InfraBridge); Invenergy Transmission LLC holds Grain Belt Express; Invenergy Renewables Operating I LLC borrows the USD 1.5 billion revolver; Invenergy Thermal Operating I LLC carried Moody's Ba2 rating in 2021. Leadership changed on 7 April 2026: Polsky became Executive Chairman, Murphy CEO, and former CCO Jim Shield President of Invenergy Power.

Collection gap: Invenergy publishes no financial statements, no per-project storage list with ISO, offtaker and contract type, and no battery supplier; the 21-page press archive would not paginate, so releases between September and December 2024 were recovered by site search only. The premise handed to this dossier — 'largest private US developer' — is corrected above; the four covered dossiers that name Invenergy (AEP, Kiewit, Meta, Apex Clean Energy) are consistent with the record here: the Sycamore Riverside sale, the Grain Belt Express awards, the 1,800 MW of Meta contracts and the Cleanview wind ranking.
ecosystemRole: Invenergy is the largest developer counterparty on the buyer side of this corpus and the one that has most visibly re-weighted toward gas-for-data-centres: it sells wind and solar output to Meta, Microsoft and Verizon, sells completed gas plants to regulated utilities (AEP's Indiana Michigan Power, We Energies), awards HVDC transmission EPC to Quanta and Kiewit with Siemens Energy converters, and buys utility-scale storage for Arizona utilities and, since September 2026, a 200 MW California project. Its storage procurement is invisible in the public record — no integrator or cell supplier is named anywhere — which is itself the finding for a supplier reading this dossier.

productsAndServices.name: Utility-scale wind and solar — development, ownership and farmdown
productsAndServices.description: The heritage business and, by any measure the record supports, still the largest: Cleanview's live development-pipeline rankings (read 5 September 2026) place Invenergy second in the US overall (41,328 MW, 212 projects), second in wind (14,192 MW, 63 projects) and second in solar (22,560 MW, 124 projects), behind NextEra Energy in each table. The commercial model is to develop, contract and build, then hold or farm down: WEC Energy Group is 'majority owner' of Delilah I Solar (300 MW, Texas, commercial February 2025) and Hardin III Solar (250 MW, Ohio, commercial June 2025) with Invenergy as developer and operator; NIPSCO took Fairbanks Solar (250 MW, Indiana, commercial July 2025) under a build-transfer agreement; AEP's SWEPCO and PSO bought 1 GW of wind and solar for about USD 2.2 billion with construction financed by a Natixis-led USD 1.27 billion facility; and an Invenergy-led consortium with CDPQ and Blackstone bought AEP's 1,365 MW unregulated renewables portfolio for USD 1.5 billion enterprise value in August 2023. Named corporate offtakers in the trailing period are Meta (eight projects, 1,800 MW cumulative), Verizon (four projects, 640 MW, more than 1 GW cumulative), Microsoft (Hardin III 250 MW), Honda and Tesla (Delilah I).
highlights: Cleanview (September 2026): #2 US developer by pipeline overall, wind and solar; the company's own 'largest privately held' claim carries no third-party attribution on any page read

Meta: 791 MW added June 2025 (Yellow Wood 300 MW, Pleasant Prairie 140 MW, Decoy 155 MW, Seaway Wind 196 MW) on top of 760 MW of environmental-attribute agreements in December 2024 — 'Total MW with Meta: 1,800 MW'
Verizon: 640 MW of new virtual PPAs (Richfield 50 MW, Maple Flats 250 MW, Cadence 240 MW, Chalk Bluff 100 MW), more than 1 GW cumulative (February 2025)
Mercom (February 2025): USD 1.1 billion of construction and bridge debt for three solar projects totalling 590 MW in Ohio, Indiana and Tennessee, lenders unnamed

South Dakota PUC approved the 333 MW, about USD 750 million Philip Wind project (February 2026), described as the state's largest; PPAW 1 (350 MW, Quebec, Hydro-Québec offtake) closed CAD 1.1 billion of financing in June 2025
Illuminate USA modules are specified on Invenergy's own Ohio solar projects (Pleasant Prairie, Hardin III); Blattner is the named EPC at Pleasant Prairie
productsAndServices.positioning: The only privately owned developer in Cleanview's top ten; a full-service developer-operator (in-house development, construction, Invenergy Services operations) where Intersect and Hecate are development platforms and NextEra and Engie are utility or IPP balance sheets.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Long-term PPAs and virtual PPAs with corporates and utilities; build-transfer and majority farmdowns to utilities (NIPSCO, WEC Energy Group, SWEPCO/PSO, Dominion Energy Virginia); project-level construction debt (Natixis, Mercom-reported USD 1.1 billion) and tax-credit transfers (the AEP portfolio's USD 580 million PTC transfer with Bank of America).
targetSegments: Hyperscalers and telecoms (Meta, Microsoft, Verizon, Equinix)
Regulated utilities and public power (AEP, NIPSCO, WEC, SRP, APS, Grant County PUD, Hydro-Québec)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Meta projects due 2027 (Yellow Wood, Pleasant Prairie, Decoy) and 2028 (Seaway Wind); Verizon's Cadence Solar 2026 and Chalk Bluff 2027; Philip Wind construction from June 2026; Quincy Solar (120 MW, Washington) late 2027; Hashknife Solar (475 MW, Arizona) 2027 per POWER Magazine.

productsAndServices.name: Battery energy storage — standalone and hybrid, owned and operated
productsAndServices.category: Owned and operated BESS — contracted (utility offtake) and hybrid
productsAndServices.description: Invenergy has built batteries since Grand Ridge (Illinois, 2012, 36 MW for PJM frequency regulation) but discloses the fleet only in aggregates: '27 projects developed', '5,000 megawatt-hours of storage developed', '150 utility-scale projects in the storage development pipeline' (storage page, read September 2026); '21 storage projects totaling 556 megawatts or 1,817 megawatt-hours' company-wide in August 2024; 'more than 25 energy storage projects totaling more than 1,250 megawatts' as relayed by The Pajaronian in September 2026. The operating core is Arizona: eleven APS-contracted projects commissioned 2023–2024 (Energy-Storage.news lists Cotton Center, Desert Star, El Sol, Foothills I and II, Gila Bend I and II, Paloma, Hyder I and II and Yuma — 261 MW / 903 MWh), and SRP's March 2026 release counts 736 MW of Invenergy storage operating or under construction in the state. Named development-stage microsites total about 2.4 GW (agent arithmetic, not a company figure): Cloud Cap 1,000 MW / 4,000 MWh and Hazy Peak 700 MW / 2,800 MWh in Arizona, Lincoln Route 300 MW / 1,200 MWh in Iowa, Yum Yum 147 MW in Tennessee, Hardin II 105 MW / 420 MWh in Ohio, Tip Top 70 MW / 280 MWh in New Mexico, Richfield 50 MW in Maryland. The first SRP agreement, SunDog (200 MW solar plus 200 MW / 800 MWh storage, Pinal County), was announced in March 2026, and on 3 September 2026 The Pajaronian reported Invenergy taking over the 200 MW Seahawk (Minto Road) project in Santa Cruz County, California from New Leaf Energy.
highlights: Chemistry stated as lithium iron phosphate (company blog; the 2018 MidAmerican 1 MW / 4 MWh unit); no integrator, cell maker or PCS supplier is named in any first-party or third-party source read — a collection gap
ISO membership is never stated by the company; by geography the Arizona fleet sits in the APS and SRP balancing areas (WECC, non-ISO), Grand Ridge in PJM, Lincoln Route in MISO, Seahawk in CAISO

The El Sol figures conflict: 50 MW / 200 MWh per the August 2024 release and Energy-Storage.news, '250 megawatts / 1,250+ megawatt-hours' on the project microsite — the company does not reconcile them
Invenergy Services lists 'Storage (400+ MW)' across '19 storage projects' in its operated fleet
Contract types are disclosed only as 'power purchase agreement' (APS, Yuma) and 'agreement' (SRP, SunDog); no tolling, RA or merchant designation appears
productsAndServices.positioning: A utility-contracted Southwest storage owner rather than a merchant or hyperscaler-facing storage platform: on the record, every operating battery serves an Arizona utility or a wind-solar co-location. Against Aypa (about 6.5 GW contracted) and Plus Power, Invenergy's disclosed storage fleet is small; against its own 38 GW, it is a rounding error the company says it intends to grow ('150 utility-scale projects' in pipeline).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility PPAs and energy-storage agreements (APS, SRP); build-own-operate with Invenergy Services as operator; late-stage acquisitions (Seahawk) alongside greenfield microsites.
targetSegments: Hybrid additions to its own wind and solar sites
productsAndServices.roadmap: SunDog (SRP) date not stated; Cloud Cap, Hazy Peak, Hardin II, Tip Top, Richfield and Yum Yum are in 'site characterization and permitting'; Lincoln Route in 'preliminary studies and land campaign'; Seahawk under new ownership from September 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Natural gas and data-centre power — Invenergy Power
productsAndServices.category: Generation — gas plants developed for utilities and large loads
productsAndServices.description: Gas is the fastest-moving line and, since 7 April 2026, has its own unit: 'Chief Commercial Officer Jim Shield will become President of Invenergy Power, which will oversee the company's growing natural gas and data center development.' The model is develop-and-sell to regulated utilities facing data-centre load: Indiana Michigan Power (AEP) filed with the IURC in April 2026 to acquire the 918 MW Sycamore Riverside Energy Center (Sullivan County, about USD 500 million per Inside INdiana Business, ownership transfer March 2029, IURC decision expected end-2026); We Energies filed with the Wisconsin PSC in November 2025 to acquire Foundry Ridge (Walworth County) and Red Oak Ridge (Kenosha County, 1.1 GW) — WPR gives the figures as USD 564.2 million and USD 1.77 billion — to serve the Microsoft Mount Pleasant and Vantage Port Washington campuses; and on 31 August 2026 Invenergy filed engineering plans for two more Wisconsin plants at Brillion (Union Depot 750 MW baseload, Forest Junction 1,200 MW peaker) for We Energies service by December 2031. In Arizona a February 2026 precedent agreement makes Invenergy the anchor shipper on Tallgrass gas infrastructure for 'as many as three new natural gas-fired power plants' in Maricopa and Yuma Counties. The June 2026 Interior settlement (USD 765 million for four offshore leases) was explicitly redirected to 'natural gas-fired power plants in Indiana, Wisconsin, Iowa, Kansas, and Missouri and geothermal'.
highlights: Historic gas fleet: Lackawanna Energy Center 1,485 MW (Pennsylvania, 2019), Nelson (Illinois), Ector County (ERCOT, 330 MW), Grays Harbor, St. Clair, Cannon Falls, Spindle Hill, Hardee — 2,680 MW net in the Invenergy Thermal Operating I LLC portfolio Moody's rated Ba2 in 2021
The gas portfolio sits in Invenergy Clean Power LLC, 50/50 with AMP Capital (now InfraBridge) since May 2018

NVIDIA / Emerald AI 'flexible AI factories' programme (March 2026): Invenergy joins AES, Constellation, NextEra, Nscale and Vistra around the Vera Rubin DSX reference design; the April 2026 blog describes 'a portfolio of AI factory-ready powered sites' from 'edge and distributed inference deployments to multi-GW campuses' — no site is named
The Daily Reporter's August 2026 figures for the two earlier Wisconsin plants are transposed against WPR's November 2025 report; WPR's are carried here
Sullivan County, Indiana hosts four Invenergy projects: Sycamore Riverside, Grain Belt Express, Fairbanks and Trade Post
productsAndServices.positioning: A gas developer that sells the plant to the utility at commissioning rather than an IPP that keeps merchant gas — the opposite of Vistra, NRG and Talen, which are contracting existing fleets to data centres. Invenergy's edge is siting and permitting speed at its existing project sites (Foundry Ridge at the Darien solar site; Sycamore beside its own Fairbanks and Grain Belt work).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Build-and-transfer to regulated utilities under CPCN filings (IURC, Wisconsin PSC); own-and-operate via Invenergy Clean Power for the legacy fleet; gas supply precedent agreements (Tallgrass).
targetSegments: Regulated utilities with hyperscaler load (AEP, WEC Energy)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Sycamore Riverside to I&M March 2029; Foundry Ridge end-2028 and Red Oak Ridge end-2029 per WPR; Union Depot and Forest Junction PSC application October 2026, construction Q4 2027, completion late 2031; Arizona gas plants undated.

productsAndServices.name: Transmission — Grain Belt Express and the HVDC portfolio
productsAndServices.description: Grain Belt Express is an about 800-mile, 5,000 MW, 600 kV HVDC line from western Kansas through Missouri and Illinois to Indiana, connecting four grid regions, at a stated USD 11 billion; Phase 1 is about 530 miles between converter stations in Kansas and Missouri with construction 'anticipated 2026' and, per ConstructConnect, completion in 2029. Contractor awards of USD 1.7 billion combined went to Quanta Services and Kiewit Energy Group in May 2025; Siemens Energy is the HVDC technology partner (January 2023), Prysmian supplies up to 12,500 miles of E3X conductor and Hubbell about USD 70 million of hardware. All four state approvals are in hand (Indiana 2013, Kansas 2019 amended 2023, Missouri 2019 amended 2023, Illinois 2023), the Missouri Supreme Court denied review in January 2025, and the Illinois Supreme Court upheld the ICC certificate 6–0 on 23 January 2026 while remanding three constitutional claims. The Department of Energy terminated its USD 4.9 billion conditional loan guarantee for Phase 1 on 23 July 2025; the company now describes the line as 'privately financed'. Missouri Attorney General Andrew Bailey issued a civil investigative demand on 2 July 2025 and asked the PSC to re-examine the certificate; Grain Belt petitioned Cole County Circuit Court to quash it. The company also lists Cimarron Link (1,900 MW, Oklahoma Panhandle to Jenks), New Mexico North Path (4,000 MW, with the state's RETA) and the operating Cardal line in Uruguay (55 km 500 kV, UTE 30-year lease, February 2024); '11 gigawatts of new transmission capacity in development'. Clean Path NY (175 miles, 3,800 MW, USD 11 billion, with energyRe and NYPA) lost its NYSERDA Tier 4 contract by mutual termination in November 2024 after the developers sought higher payments; NYPA petitioned the PSC in January 2025 to keep the project alive as a priority transmission project.
highlights: Landowner easements: more than USD 105 million executed, USD 19 million paid, USD 86 million due at construction; 'over 1,500 voluntary agreements' (July 2025 letter to Secretary Wright)
Anchor customers: MOPEP's 39 Missouri municipal utilities under transmission service agreements ('$12.8 million in annual energy savings')
An amended interconnection agreement between Grain Belt Express LLC and ITC Great Plains was filed by SPP at FERC on 23 January 2026 (ER26-1106)
Fortune (August 2025): Invenergy argued the line would carry 'coal, gas, and nuclear' as well as renewables; Axios reported a planned gas-plant connection in July 2025
FERC (October 2025) denied Invenergy Energy Management's complaint against PJM (EL23-29) and granted in part Invenergy Transmission's complaint against MISO on merchant transmission in MTEP (EL22-83)
productsAndServices.positioning: The only US developer building a multi-state merchant HVDC line at this scale; what transmission ownership buys is the right to site generation and load where the line lands — a capability no other BESS-side developer in this corpus has.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Transmission service agreements with municipal and public-power buyers, FERC-approved open-access tariff; EPC to Quanta and Kiewit; private financing after the DOE guarantee was withdrawn.
targetSegments: Load-serving entities in MISO, PJM and SPP
Data-centre developers seeking interregional capacity (per company statements)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Phase 1 construction from 2026, completion 2029 (ConstructConnect); Phase 2 (Missouri to Indiana) unscheduled; Cimarron Link in routing and environmental review; North Path undated.

productsAndServices.name: Operations, manufacturing and new technologies — Invenergy Services, Illuminate USA, hydrogen, geothermal, offshore exit
productsAndServices.description: Invenergy Services is the operations arm ('Storage (400+ MW)', '19 storage projects'; the natural-gas page cites '140 operational natural gas facilities' and '70 gigawatts' that appear to describe the serviced fleet rather than owned assets — the page does not say). Illuminate USA, an affiliate, runs a 1.1 million-square-foot solar-module plant in Pataskala, Ohio ('over 1,600 associates', 'over 13 million solar panels', eight lines) and named Art Fletcher CEO in April 2026. Sauk Valley Hydrogen (Rock Falls, Illinois, about 40 tonnes a year, Ohmium electrolysers, Aether Fuels offtake) reached commercial operation in March 2025. Offshore wind has been exited: Leading Light Wind (2.4 GW, New Jersey, with energyRe) was cancelled in November 2025 for 'financial, supply chain and regulatory obstacles', and on 17 June 2026 Interior agreed to pay USD 765 million — the original lease prices — to cancel four leases (New York Bight OCS-A 0542 USD 645 million, Morro Bay USD 112 million, two Gulf of Maine leases about USD 9 million). Invenergy Geothermal Development holds 45 BLM leases across about 144,000 acres in Utah, Idaho, Nevada and New Mexico and plans enhanced-geothermal drilling from late 2026; no geothermal plant operates yet.
highlights: Reactivate (community solar) and Energize Capital (venture fund) are listed as ventures on invenergy.com
'Raised over $75 billion in capital' since 2001 (April 2026 boilerplate) and 'over $500 million invested in American communities' in 2025
Prysmian's Williamsport expansion and Hubbell's Grain Belt order are framed by the company as domestic supply-chain reshoring
productsAndServices.positioning: An integrated developer with its own module plant, operator and early-stage technology bets — the diversification that lets the capital go where policy points (gas and geothermal in 2026, offshore wind in 2022).
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Operations and maintenance contracts (Invenergy Services); module supply to Invenergy projects and third parties (Illuminate USA); hydrogen offtake (Aether Fuels).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Enhanced geothermal drilling later in 2026 (Canary Media); Illuminate USA sustainability reporting and glass sourcing (SOLARCYCLE, August 2025).

The IRG Acquisition Holdings purchase of AEP's 1,365 MW portfolio closed in August 2023 with a USD 580 million production-tax-credit transfer arranged by Bank of America, described as 'the first announced large scale transferability transaction to close'.

policyExposure.exposure: Invenergy monetises credits through transfers and tax equity at portfolio scale: the August 2023 purchase of AEP's 1,365 MW portfolio carried a USD 580 million production-tax-credit transfer arranged by Bank of America Securities, described in Invenergy's release as 'the first announced large scale transferability transaction to close since the passing of the Inflation Reduction Act'. Its Illuminate USA affiliate is a domestic module manufacturer whose output is specified on Invenergy's Ohio projects, which bears on domestic-content bonuses.
policyExposure.mitigation: Illuminate USA (Pataskala, Ohio, eight lines) and the Prysmian and Hubbell supply agreements are framed by the company as domestic supply chain.

policyExposure.exposure: Jim Murphy told the ACORE conference in June 2025 that the FEOC provision was 'unworkable' because 'the supply chain can not support that'. Treasury's 95-page draft guidance of 12 February 2026 deferred the 'effective control' question and set 4 July 2026 as the begin-construction deadline for wind and solar to keep credits — the deadline that governs Invenergy's 2027–2028 Meta and Verizon projects. No Invenergy statement on how its unnamed battery suppliers sit under the rule was found.

The USD 4.9 billion conditional loan guarantee for Grain Belt Express Phase 1 (issued 25 November 2024) was terminated on 23 July 2025; DOE said the conditions 'are unlikely to be met and it is not critical for the federal government to have a role'. Latitude Media reported that career LPO attorneys had advised the cancellation would breach the contract. The company's response was that the line would proceed 'privately financed'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Private financing on the USD 11 billion line; the USD 1.7 billion EPC awards and 95% of Phase 1 easements were already executed.

policyExposure.exposure: Interior agreed to pay Invenergy USD 765 million — matching the original lease prices — to cancel four offshore leases (OCS-A 0542 in the New York Bight, a Morro Bay lease and two Gulf of Maine leases), the third such settlement after TotalEnergies. BOEM's lease page records the cancellation as 'contingent upon Invenergy demonstrating necessary investments in U.S. conventional energy development'; Invenergy committed the proceeds to gas plants in Indiana, Wisconsin, Iowa, Kansas and Missouri and to geothermal.
policyExposure.mitigation: Redeployment into gas plants for utilities and 45 geothermal leases (about 144,000 acres).

policyExposure.regime: State siting and certificate law (Missouri, Illinois, Kansas, Indiana)
policyExposure.exposure: Grain Belt Express holds certificates in all four states; the Illinois Supreme Court upheld the ICC certificate 6–0 on 23 January 2026, the Missouri Supreme Court denied review of the PSC's Tiger Connector approval in January 2025, and the Missouri Court of Appeals held in October 2024 that a county cannot block the line by refusing road crossings. The Missouri Attorney General's July 2025 civil investigative demand and request that the PSC re-examine the certificate are the live challenges; PSC counsel has said the certificates 'cannot be revoked by the commission'.
policyExposure.mitigation: Petition to quash the CID in Cole County Circuit Court (July 2025).

policyExposure.exposure: Grain Belt Express is a FAST-41 covered project (20 February 2024) with a DOE environmental impact statement for Phase 1 in development; in September 2024 Invenergy asked DOE to 'significantly narrow' the proposed Midwest-Plains national-interest corridor. FERC in October 2025 granted in part Invenergy Transmission's complaint against MISO on the treatment of merchant transmission in MTEP (EL22-83).

financials.commentary: What can be said with confidence: about USD 4 billion of Blackstone equity since 2022, a majority position held by CDPQ and management, a USD 1.5 billion corporate revolver, and project financings in the USD 1–1.3 billion range per portfolio. Aggregator claims of a USD 20 billion-plus implied valuation and a 2025 secondary sale have no primary source and are excluded.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Invenergy's 'largest privately held developer' claim is true only on the pipeline measure and only among non-utility developers. Basis: Cleanview's live rankings (5 September 2026) place it second to NextEra Energy in every table (overall 41,328 MW against 68,229 MW), and S&P Global's 2023 ranking had the same order; no independent source names Invenergy first among private developers, and the phrase appears only in Invenergy's, Blackstone's and I&M's own text. The premise handed to this dossier is corrected to: second-largest US developer by pipeline, largest privately owned.

(High confidence) We assess that the ownership stack is unchanged since June 2023 — CDPQ (52.4% economic ownership of Invenergy Renewables LLC after 2018), Blackstone Infrastructure Partners (about USD 4 billion into Invenergy Renewables Holdings LLC across 2022–2023) and management as managing member — and that the gas portfolio sits separately in Invenergy Clean Power LLC with InfraBridge. Basis: the company's releases and capabilities page, CDPQ's 2018 release, Blackstone's 2022 release as mirrored by CDPQ; no 2024–2026 stake sale, recapitalisation, bond or rating action on the holding company was found. Aggregator claims of a USD 20 billion-plus valuation are unsourced and rejected.

(High confidence) We assess that Invenergy has re-weighted its growth capital toward gas plants sold to regulated utilities for data-centre load. Basis: the Invenergy Power unit created 7 April 2026 'to oversee the company's growing natural gas and data center development'; I&M's CPCN filing for the 918 MW Sycamore Riverside plant; We Energies' filings for Foundry Ridge and Red Oak Ridge (about USD 2.3 billion combined per WPR) and the August 2026 Brillion plans for another 1.95 GW; the Tallgrass anchor-shipper agreement; and the company's own statement that the USD 765 million offshore settlement funds gas and geothermal. The model is build-and-transfer at commissioning, not merchant gas.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that storage remains a utility-contracted Southwest business inside Invenergy rather than a merchant or hyperscaler-facing platform, and that its true size is between the company's '5,000 MWh developed' and SRP's '736 MW' Arizona figure. Basis: every operating battery a source names serves APS or SRP or is a hybrid addition to an Invenergy wind or solar site; the named development microsites (about 2.4 GW) are in 'site characterization and permitting' with no offtaker; the September 2026 Seahawk takeover is the first named CAISO storage asset. The judgment is moderate because the company discloses no per-project list and the '150 utility-scale projects' pipeline figure cannot be tested.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that Grain Belt Express will reach Phase 1 construction on private capital but on a slower schedule than 'anticipated 2026', and that its financing is now the single largest execution risk in the portfolio. Basis: the USD 1.7 billion Quanta/Kiewit awards, Siemens Energy, Prysmian and Hubbell contracts, 95%-acquired easements, the SPP-filed ITC Great Plains interconnection agreement (January 2026) and the Illinois Supreme Court win argue for proceeding; the DOE guarantee's termination, the Missouri Attorney General's investigation and the absence of any announced private financing at USD 11 billion argue for delay. Cuts against: the March 2026 Energies Media report that the four state approvals are 'the prerequisite to move the project into the construction and financing phases' implies financing is not yet closed.

(Low confidence) Trade press and the company's own blog say Invenergy is marketing 'AI factory-ready powered sites' up to 'multi-GW campuses' under the NVIDIA / Emerald AI programme. No site, customer, capacity or contract has been published; treat the data-centre siting business as an announced intent, not a pipeline. Collection gap: whether any of the Wisconsin, Indiana or Arizona gas plants is contractually tied to a named hyperscaler campus beyond the utility filings' references to Microsoft Mount Pleasant and Vantage Port Washington.

Collection gap: no battery integrator, cell supplier, PCS vendor or storage EPC is named in any Invenergy release, microsite, counterparty release or trade-press article read; the only chemistry statement is 'lithium iron phosphate'. Mark Delaney's Renewable Engineering and Procurement seat (new on the leadership page in 2026) is the procurement counterpart a supplier would approach. Indicators to watch: (1) a Wisconsin PSC decision on Foundry Ridge and Red Oak Ridge (application filed November 2025) and the IURC's end-2026 Sycamore Riverside order — approvals confirm the gas-to-utility model and its pricing; a denial would strand development capital the settlement proceeds were meant to recycle; (2) a Grain Belt Express financing announcement (bank group, bond or equity partner) before Phase 1 construction — its absence through mid-2027 would indicate the DOE termination was fatal to the 2026 schedule; (3) any Invenergy release naming a battery supplier or an ISO-level storage total, or a CAISO record for Seahawk — the first would close the largest collection gap in this dossier; (4) Treasury's final FEOC rule and the 4 July 2026 begin-construction record for the 2027 Meta and Verizon projects — a project dropping from the Meta list would show the deadline bit; (5) Illuminate USA output and any Invenergy storage project specifying domestic cells — the test of whether the module affiliate's playbook is repeated in batteries; (6) a Blackstone or CDPQ disclosure of a stake change, or a holding-company rating — either would replace the ownership judgment's 2023 baseline.
